The twist vectors are
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:twists}
 v_1=\widehat\gamma+2\widehat u-4\widehat w,
 \qquad
 v_2=-\widehat\gamma-3\widehat u+3\widehat w.
\end{equation}
Direct multiplication using \eqref{eq:A12} gives
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:twist-invariant}
 A_1v_1=v_1,\qquad A_2v_2=v_2.
\end{equation}
The invariant first-coordinate functional introduced above satisfies
\[
 \gamma(\widehat\gamma)=1,
 \qquad
 \gamma(\widehat u)=\gamma(\widehat w)
 =\gamma(\widehat\delta)=0.
\]
Then

\Lambda_{\tor}=\Z\langle\widehat w,\widehat\delta\rangle,
 \qquad
 \overline\Lambda=\Lambda/\Lambda_{\tor}
   =\Z\langle\widehat\gamma,\widehat u\rangle,
\]
write $\Omega_a=[Z_a\mid I_2]$. The nonconstant
$2\times2$ period block has the form
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:cusp-decomposition}
 Z_a=sB_0+C_a(q),
 \qquad
 B_0=
 \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 C_a(q)=C_0(q)+aE_{21},
\end{equation}
where $C_0$ is holomorphic on a disc $D_{\varepsilon_0}$ about $q=0$ and
$E_{21}$ has a single $1$ in row $2$, column $1$.
To verify the decomposition, let $b=\beta_0+\tau$. The proof of
\cref{prop:period-data-existence} shows that $b$ and $\mu$ are
$g_0$-invariant and holomorphic in $q=t_c$ at $0$, and that
$\tau=s+h(q)$. Hence the displayed period matrix gives
\[
 C_0(q)=\begin{pmatrix}6\mu(q)&h(q)\\
                       b(q)-h(q)&\mu(q)\end{pmatrix},
\]
which is holomorphic at $q=0$. The same proposition computes
$R_{g_0}=I_2$, and the additive parameter contributes $aE_{21}$.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:alpoge-member}
Let $(X^{\mathrm A},f^{\mathrm A})$ be the compact pair of
Alp\"oge~\cite[Construction~6.1]{AlpogeS6}, with its specified twists
$v_1=\widehat\gamma+2\widehat u-4\widehat w$ and
$v_2=-\widehat\gamma-3\widehat u+3\widehat w$, and untranslated cusp
gluing.
For its chosen admissible period function $\beta^{\mathrm A}$, there is a
unique constant $a_{\mathrm A}\in\mathcal A$ for which
$\beta^{\mathrm A}=\beta_0+a_{\mathrm A}$. For this parameter there is an
isomorphism of pairs
\[
 (X^{\mathrm A},f^{\mathrm A})\cong(X_{a_{\mathrm A}},f_{a_{\mathrm A}})
 \quad\text{over }B.
\]
